name: Papez circuit and limbic connections
summary: The classical memory circuit runs from the hippocampus through the fornix to the mammillary bodies, from there by the mammillothalamic tract to the anterior thalamic nuclei, on to the cingulate gyrus, and back through the cingulum bundle and entorhinal cortex to the hippocampus. Every station is a site of clinical amnesia: the hippocampus in Alzheimer disease, anoxia and herpes encephalitis, the fornix in surgery, the mammillary bodies in thiamine deficiency, the anterior and mediodorsal thalamus in stroke, and the cingulate in tumors. The amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex and mediodorsal thalamus form a parallel limbic loop for emotion and social behavior.

origin.note: Hippocampal formation (subiculum) with input from the entorhinal cortex, which collects from the association cortices.

neuronChain.synapse: anterior thalamic nuclei via the mammillothalamic tract
cingulate gyrus via the anterior limb of the internal capsule

waypoints.note: cingulum bundle to the entorhinal cortex

termination: Hippocampus (closing the loop), with outputs to the prefrontal cortex and the septal nuclei, and from the amygdala to the hypothalamus and brainstem for autonomic and behavioral responses.

lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Anterograde amnesia with preserved remote memory and intelligence

pearls: Memory loss for new events with intact reasoning is the Papez circuit; the lesion can be anywhere along it
Thiamine deficiency and third ventricular surgery injure the same circuit at different stations
Unilateral lesions cause material-specific loss: verbal on the left, visuospatial on the right
